question.text: A Cat III AIF maintains multiple Series within the same Class of Units. Why does the Series NAV per unit differ across Series, even though they hold the same underlying portfolio?

answer.text: Custodian fees are charged only to the senior Series
SEBI requires a 10% haircut on later Series for dilution
Differential terms of subscription (fees, drawdown timing) allocated at series level cause Series Expenses and Series Net Assets to diverge
Each Series holds a different subset of the portfolio

explanation.text: The Logic: Even with the same underlying portfolio, Series can carry differential fee structures, expense allocations, and other differential rights. Series NAV is computed as Series Assets less Series Liabilities and Series Expenses, where the expenses depend on those differential rights — so each Series accrues a different fee drag and yields a different NAV per unit. The Trap: Option A introduces an unsupported custodian-fee allocation rule. Option B fabricates a SEBI dilution haircut. Option D misconceives 'Series' as portfolio segregation — Series share the same investment portfolio. Note: The 'same portfolio, different fee/expense allocation' design is what makes Series NAV diverge — it is a structural feature of multi-Series Cat III funds, not an accounting error.
